Twitter’s traditional bird icon was booted and replaced with an image of a Shiba Inu, an apparent nod to dogecoin, the joke cryptocurrency that CEO Elon Musk is being sued over.

Musk addressed the change Monday afternoon, tweeting, “as promised” above an image of a year-old conversation in which another user suggested that Musk “just buy Twitter” and “change the bird logo to a doge.”.

According to recent reports, elon Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out one account.

The doge logo appeared on the site two days after Musk asked a judge to throw out a $258 billion racketeering lawsuit accusing him of running a pyramid scheme to support the dogecoin, according to Reuters.

Lawyers for Musk and Tesla called the lawsuit by dogecoin investors a “fanciful work of fiction” over Musk’s “innocuous and often silly tweets.”.

It wasn’t clear whether the logo change was permanent. Musk has been known to use Twitter to troll both his fans and his critics.

It has been revealed that the price of dogecoin, which is typically volatile, was up more than 20% over the past 24 hours, to about 9 cents. It was trading just under 8 cents Monday morning.

Recent findings suggest that dogecoin was created December 6, 2013, by a pair of software engineers — as a joke. The name is a nod to the “doge” meme that became popular a decade ago. Its Shiba Inu mascot mimicks that meme: a dog surrounded by a bunch of Comic Sans text in broken English.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union.
  • Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.
  • Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union.

Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.

Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.

Huerta’s casket was escorted inside the Dignity Health arena for the interfaith memorial service as Mariachi Lindas Mexicanas played next to it.

Huerta, a feminist icon who co-founded the United Farm Workers (UFW) in 1962, died on 28 October aged 96.

Attenders came from all over California to pay their respects. Rosa de la Cruz, a 44-year-old farm worker who lives in Tulare, about an hour north of Bakersfield, remarked she wanted to pay her respects in person.

The world-renowned labor rights leader and activist means “a great deal”, de la Cruz remarked, “because if it hadn’t been for her, there wouldn’t be many benefits for the people who work in the fields.”.

The week was filled with events dedicated to Huerta’s memory, her courage, resilience and her impact on the community.

On Monday, Huerta was honored in Sacramento by state government officials including Monique Limón, the senate president pro tempore, Robert Rivas, the assembly speaker, Xavier Becerra, the California governor-elect, and community leaders in a historic ceremony.

It has been revealed that huerta became the first female, first Latino and first non-elected leader to lie in honor at the state capitol. Her casket was escorted in after a march organized by local unions.

Recent findings suggest that “Our mother devoted her entire life to fighting injustice and lifting up communities too often left out and treated unfairly,” mentioned Huerta’s family. “As a lifelong organizer, her activism has been a source of inspiration and empowerment for people around the world.”.

For more than six decades, Huerta spearheaded historic boycotts, fought tirelessly for farm workers’ rights, women’s equality and environmental justice, and coined the enduring national rally cry, “¡Sí, se puede!”.

Recent findings suggest that huerta has received numerous honors including the Eleanor Roosevelt Human Rights Awards. In 2012, Barack Obama awarded Huerta the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor.

The two-day tribute started on Thursday evening with a public rosary and vigil in Bakersfield, where she had lived since 1990.

It has been revealed that friday’s interfaith memorial service and celebration of life began with an opening blessing by Aztec dancers. There were performances from music groups Los Lobos, Ozomatli, Las Cafeteras, Nancy Sanchez and Trio los Dados. Rob Bonta, the California attorney general, was among the speakers on Friday.

“Dolores Huerta is irreplaceable and her loss is something I think people are still, including me, getting our heads around,” Bonta stated. “To the world, she is an icon and a giant and a legend. For me, she was also a friend and a mentor and a counselor. Someone I texted with and called and sought advice from and leaned on as I rolled out my career and had my career in elected public office.”.

“Her loss is immeasurable. She is irreplaceable but she leaves a legacy of fighting for justice,” Bonta said.

Ten of Huerta’s adult children took the stage to share personal anecdotes about Huerta’s life, emphasizing her skills as an organizer, political strategist and motivational speaker. Her children recounted her dedication to social justice, her love for jazz, and her humility despite her significant contributions.

“While there is much to celebrate in our recent victories, there is still so much work to be done,” noted Huerta’s daughter Camila Chavez. “People may expect us to fill her shoes, but she is going to be buried with her shoes. Like Zapata said: ‘I’d rather live on my feet than die on my knees.’ It’s going to take all of us here to fill those shoes.”.

According to recent reports, her legacy will continue through the work and empowering mission of the Dolores Huerta Foundation. In 2003, Huerta founded the grassroots community organization to create leadership opportunities for community members, while organizing underserved communities, and pursuing social justice.

Huerta kept on working even as a nonagenarian, dedicating her life as an organizer.

In the Central valley, Huerta supported minorities to run for office to make a difference at the local, state and federal level. In a 2022 speech, Huerta encouraged fresh US citizens to fulfill their civic responsibilities, especially voting.

For her 94th birthday, Huerta asked people to help her celebrate by getting others involved in elections either by talking to somebody about voting and about registering to vote.

Huerta urged uninsured Latinos and Californians to enroll in health coverage with the passage of the Affordable Care Act partnering with Covered California to spread the message. Huerta also had several schools named after her throughout the state. Last year, Huerta joined Central valley educators to demand David Valadao, a US representative from California, defend funding for schools.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Thursday's meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" in Berlin sent a strong signal to Moscow that it was time to take negotiations to end the war in Ukraine seriously.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to DW during a visit to the South Caucasus, Wadephul described the summit as the largest meeting of Ukraine's supporters so far. The meeting represents the 18th set of high-level talks among the coalition's members.

He stated it demonstrated that allies remained firmly behind Kyiv in the fifth year of Russia's war and were ready to do "what was necessary to ensure Ukraine could negotiate from a position of strength.".

"The summit itself is already a success," he told DW.

Wadephul also welcomed the US initiative to restart peace negotiations. After nine months without progress, an initial meeting had taken place in Abu Dhabi, with a follow-up round planned and European participation expected.

"We are also preparing for the possibility that the negotiations will not be successful and that, over the coming winter, we will have to continue supplying Ukraine with heating, electricity and all essential supplies, including water," he mentioned.

"And we will continue to stand by Ukraine militarily.".

He stressed that any peace agreement must include security guarantees to protect Ukraine against future Russian attacks.

In earlier comments during his trip to the South Caucasus, Wadephul said that Ukraine and Europe must be involved in any negotiations over the future of Ukraine.

Wadephul did, however, welcome the trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

"Every conversation that takes place is a good conversation," he told DW during a visit to Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

Later on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated he had invited Europeans to Moscow for talks on the potential structure of future talks to end the war.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
  • In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month announced that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.
  • Industry observers note that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” stated the HDP in a statement on March 23.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month announced that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.

Industry observers note that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” stated the HDP in a statement on March 23. “To fulfill our historical responsibility against the one-man rule, we will not field a presidential candidate in (the) May 14 elections.”.

According to recent reports, it is a twist of irony for the Turkish strongman, who spent the better half of the past decade cracking down on the party after it began chipping away at his voter base. Its former leader Selahattin Demirtas has been in prison for nearly seven years and the party faces possible closure by a court for suspected collusion with the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and affiliated groups. But its influence may nonetheless determine the course of Turkey’s politics.

Recent findings suggest that the HDP’s decision not to field a candidate came just three days after head of the Republican People’s Party (CHP) Kemal Kilicdaroglu, Erdogan’s main rival, visited the party’s co-chairs. He told reporters that the solution to Turkey’s problems, “including the Kurdish problem” lies in parliament,” according to Turkish media.

Industry observers note that kilicdaroglu, who represents the six-party Nation Alliance opposition bloc, is the strongest contender to run against Erdogan in years. And while the HDP hasn’t yet unveiled whether it will put its weight behind him, analysts say it is the kingmaker in the elections.

Erdogan's 'polar opposite' wants to replace him as president of Turkey.

“It was a carefully crafted political discourse,” Hisyar Ozsoy, deputy co-chair of the HDP and a member of parliament from the predominantly Kurdish province of Diyarbakir, told CNN. “We are not going to have our own candidate, and we will leave it to the international community to interpret it the way they wish.”.

Experts say the crackdown on the HDP is rooted in the threat it poses to Erdogan politically, as well as its position as one of the main parties representing Turkey’s Kurds, an ethnic minority from which a separatist militant movement has emerged.

According to recent reports, the party and the Kurdish people have had a complicated relationship with Erdogan. The leader courted the Kurds in earlier years by granting them more rights and reversing restrictions on the use of their language. Relations with the HDP were also cordial once, as Erdogan worked with the party on a brief peace process with the PKK.

But ties between Erdogan and the HDP later turned sour, and the HDP fell under a sweeping crackdown aimed at the PKK and their affiliates.

Kurds are the biggest minority in Turkey, making up between 15% and 20% of the population, according to Minority Rights Group International.

It is unclear if the HDP will endorse Kilicdaroglu, but analysts say that the deliberate distance may be beneficial for the opposition candidate.

The accusations against the HDP place it in a precarious position during the elections. It currently faces a case in Turkey’s Constitutional Court over suspected ties to the PKK, which is designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. Knowing it may be banned at any moment, its candidates are running under the Green Left Party in parliament.

If the opposition is seen as allying with the HDP, Erdogan’s AK Party may use its influence in the media to discredit it as being pro-PKK, noted Murat Somer, a political science professor at Koc University in Istanbul and author of Return to Point Zero, a book on the Turkish-Kurdish question in Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that the HDP’s threat to Erdogan’s hold on power became apparent after the June 2015 election, the first general election it participated in. It won 13% of the seats, denying the ruling AK Party its majority for the first time since 2002. Erdogan, however, called a snap election five months later, which led to a drop in the HDP’s support to 10.7%, as well as the restoration of the AK Party’s overall majority.

Recent findings suggest that “They are a kingmaker in these elections because the HDP gets about half of the votes of the Kurdish population in Turkey,” said Somer, adding that the other, more conservative Kurdish voters have traditionally voted for Erdogan’s AK Party. And last month, the Free Cause Party (HUDA-PAR), a tiny Kurdish-Islamist party announced support for Erdogan in the elections. The party has never won seats in parliament.

Erdogan's political fate may rest on his response to the earthquake.

The HDP knows that its position is key to the outcome of next month’s vote, but that it’s also in a delicate situation.

“We want to play the game wisely, and we need to be very careful,” said Ozsoy, adding that the party wants to avoid a “contaminated political climate” where the elections are polarized “between a very ugly ultra-nationalist discourse against Kilicdaroglu and others.”.

The party was founded in 2012 with a number of aims, said Ozsoy, one of which was “peaceful and democratic resolution of the Kurdish conflict.”.

Somer stated that the party was seen to be “an initiative” of the PKK, which later led to a heavy government crackdown on it in the name of counterterrorism.

Its former leader Demirtas remains an influential figure.

The Turkish government has been trying to link the HDP to the PKK but has so far failed to prove “a real connection,” said Asli Aydintasbas, a visiting fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC.

Sources indicate that A post-Erdogan Turkey may give some breathing space to the Kurds and Kurdish-dominated parties in Turkey, Aydintasbas told CNN, noting that many Kurdish voters have recently left Erdogan’s camp. “For HDP, this is more than just an ideological choice,” she said. “It’s a matter of survival.”.

Ozsoy indicates his party understands what’s at stake, not only for Turkey’s Kurds but for all its minorities.

“We are aware of our responsibility here. We are aware of our role. We know we are in a kingmaker position,” the HDP lawmaker said.

Two women arrested for not wearing hijab following ‘yogurt attack’.

Two women were arrested in Iran for failing to wear the hijab in public, after a man threw a tub of yogurt at them at a store in the city of Shandiz on Thursday, according to Mizan News Agency, the state-run outlet for Iran’s judiciary.

Oil prices surge after OPEC+ producers announce surprise cuts.

Oil prices spiked Monday after OPEC+ producers unexpectedly revealed that they would cut output. Brent crude, the global benchmark, jumped 5.31% to $84.13 a barrel, while WTI, the US benchmark, rose 5.48% to $79.83. Both were the sharpest price rises in almost a year. The collective output cut by the nine members of OPEC+ totals 1.66 million barrels per day.

Iran blames Israel for the killing of second IRGC officer, vows to respond.

A second Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) officer died following an attack in Syria on Friday, according to Iranian state media on Sunday. Iranian state media said the Iranian military adviser died after an Israeli attack near the Syrian capital Damascus left him wounded. The attack also killed another IRGC officer. In a tweet on Sunday, Iranian government spokesman Ali Bahadori Jahromi said the alleged Israeli attack wouldn’t go unanswered. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Nasser Kanaani said on Sunday that Iran has the right to respond to “state terrorism.”.

Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani, who has been touring the Middle East, spoke to CNN’s Becky Anderson about his support for the protests in his homeland, saying that he used his standup comedy platform to highlight the “brutality against the Iranian people.”.

“It was an opportunity for me to say, ‘let’s keep fighting,’” he remarked.

An Iranian state news outlet is gloating at what it sees as the demise of the US dollar.

Recent findings suggest that IRNA recreated a popular meme to mark China and Brazil’s decision to reportedly ditch the US dollar as an intermediary in trade, citing the Chinese state news outlet, China Daily. It demonstrates two men representing China and Brazil posing in front of a grave labelled “USD.”.

Sources indicate that the meme was pinned to the top of IRNA’s Twitter page, and was met with laughter and ridicule. “Dream on,” noted another user, pointing to the dollar’s use as the main reserve currency around the world.

China Daily noted that the agreement was part of “the rising global use of the Chinese renminbi.” It would reportedly enable China and Brazil to conduct trade and financial transactions using local currencies instead of the dollar.

CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1468 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After more than four decades of searching, physicists at CERN have finally found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay that occurs only about once in every 10 billion beauty particles.
  • Industry observers note that the evidence comes from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
  • The elusive process, called 'Bd to mu mu', has a statistical significance of 3.2 sigma.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After more than four decades of searching, physicists at CERN have finally found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay that occurs only about once in every 10 billion beauty particles. The long-awaited result could help scientists investigate a largely unexplored realm of physics where unknown particles and forces of nature may exist.

Industry observers note that the evidence comes from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Researchers at the University of Manchester played important roles in the international effort, contributing to the advanced technology that made the measurement possible.

The elusive process, called 'Bd to mu mu', has a statistical significance of 3.2 sigma. That is strong enough to qualify as evidence, but physicists will need additional data before they can officially declare a discovery. Even so, the finding marks a major milestone in a search that has lasted more than 40 years.

It also creates fresh opportunities to test the Standard Model, the leading scientific framework describing fundamental particles and how they interact. By examining this exceptionally rare decay in greater detail, researchers hope to uncover subtle clues that could eventually point toward physics beyond our current understanding.

Why Rare Particle Decays Could Reveal New Physics.

It has been revealed that the LHCb experiment specializes in studying particles that contain beauty quarks. These are heavier relatives of the up and down quarks that make up much of the ordinary matter around us.

In a recent development, when particles collide inside the Large Hadron Collider, enormous numbers of beauty quarks are produced. However, they survive for only about one and a half trillionths of a second before decaying into other particles.

Scientists study these transformations because they may reveal the influence of particles that cannot be directly observed at the collider. By measuring exactly how frequently different decays occur, physicists can search for unexpected effects that might indicate previously unknown physics.

It has been revealed that particularly rare decays offer an important advantage. Because they happen so infrequently, their rates can be especially sensitive to contributions from undiscovered particles. Even small differences between predicted and observed decay rates could provide valuable evidence of newly introduced forces or particles.

A One in 10 Billion Particle Decay.

Recent findings suggest that the newly observed signal involves a process known as 'Bd to mu mu'. During this decay, a particle containing a beauty quark transforms into two muons, which are heavier relatives of electrons.

According to theoretical predictions, this transformation should occur only about once in every 10 billion beauty particles. Despite decades of investigation, no individual experiment had previously produced convincing evidence that it occurs.

The upgraded LHCb experiment has now achieved a statistical significance of 3.2 sigma. Although this meets the standard for reporting evidence, particle physicists generally require a significance of five sigma before announcing a confirmed discovery.

Recent findings suggest that professor Chris Parkes, Head of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester, led the international LHCb collaboration during construction of its major upgrade. He also oversaw the collaboration's approval of the new findings.

He explained: "The upgraded LHCb was a major undertaking -- a fifteen-year design and construction project from a 1900 international member collaboration.

"The UK made the largest national contribution to the project, pioneering new technologies that have made today's result possible, where we probe nature at a new scale. But this is also just the start; we are planning the construction of an experiment that will exploit the capabilities of the next-generation High Luminosity LHC, probing physics at an even smaller scale.".

Parkes, who became a Fellow of the Royal Society earlier this year in recognition of his contributions to LHCb, offered a memorable comparison to illustrate just how improbable the decay is.

"This decay is remarkably unlikely; the chance of it happening is roughly like going on a romantic date and, on your very first try, finding the one perfect match for you among everyone on Earth.".

Advanced LHC Detectors Make the Breakthrough Possible.

Detecting such an uncommon event requires instruments capable of following the movements of particles with extraordinary accuracy.

One of the most key components of the upgraded LHCb experiment is a silicon pixel detector developed with major contributions from researchers in the United Kingdom. Called the Vertex Locator, it measures the paths of particles generated during collisions inside the collider.

Positioned just five millimeters from the LHC beams, the detector allows researchers to determine precisely where particles originate and where they subsequently decay.

Industry observers note that dr. Stefano De Capua, who directed detector construction at the University of Manchester, described the extensive collaboration behind the technology.

Recent findings suggest that "We worked with nearly 90 UK companies to construct this detector and trained the next generation of scientists and engineers on the novel technologies we are using. It is these detectors that we use to locate where the beauty meson was produced and pinpoint where it decayed into two muons.".

It has been revealed that the wider LHCb upgrade also allows the experiment to gather information at up to five times its previous rate. This greater capacity, together with improvements in tracking technology, is helping physicists identify events that were previously too difficult to measure reliably.

Exploring the Mysterious Zeptoverse.

Beyond confirming an exceptionally rare particle process, the result could help scientists investigate what they call the 'Zeptoverse'.

This name refers to an almost unimaginably small scale, measured in zeptometers. A single zeptometer is just a billionth of a trillionth of a meter. Physicists suspect that effects from currently unknown particles and forces could become apparent when nature is examined at these extreme scales.

For now, the fresh measurement agrees with the Standard Model. Researchers have not found evidence that the established theory is wrong, but increasingly precise measurements could reveal deviations that current experiments cannot yet detect.

Such differences would be especially significant because they could indicate where the Standard Model stops providing a complete explanation of the physical world.

Professor Conor Fitzpatrick of the University of Manchester, who serves as Deputy Physics Coordinator of the international LHCb collaboration, emphasized the importance of finally obtaining the long-sought signal.

"There has been a more than forty year long search by physicists worldwide to observe this decay. It is a golden channel to observe the effects of fresh physics from beyond our current knowledge.

"The results from this experiment are expanding our understanding of nature at its most fundamental level. We are excited to have finally seen this elusive signal and looking forward to the future discoveries that will come from our data.".

What Comes Next for CERN's Particle Research?

The upgraded LHCb experiment is expected to continue gathering a substantially larger collection of measurements into the early 2030s. With more data, physicists should be able to determine the frequency of this rare decay with much greater precision.

Researchers are also planning another major upgrade that could increase data collection rates by an additional factor of ten. This would improve their ability to investigate extremely rare particle processes and search for the effects of unknown particles at even smaller distance scales.

Professor Brian Cox, a particle physicist at the University of Manchester who did not participate in the experiment, highlighted how improvements in scientific instruments can lead to key advances in understanding nature.

It has been revealed that "This is an notable result and a beautiful example of how science advances. We upgrade our instruments, and we see nature in greater detail. Occasionally we see something we don't understand, and then progress is made. We cannot know whether this progress will be incremental or genuinely world-changing -- that's science! LHCb is a major scientific success.".

Sources indicate that the experiment receives funding from the Science and Technology Facilities Council, which operates within UK Research and Innovation. The UK LHCb collaboration brings together scientists from ten universities across the United Kingdom and the STFC Rutherford Appleton Laboratory.

According to recent reports, although the newly detected decay has not yet revealed any unknown particles or forces, it gives physicists a powerful latest way to search for them. After more than 40 years of effort, an extraordinarily elusive process is finally becoming accessible to detailed study, potentially bringing researchers closer to understanding some of the universe's deepest mysteries.

The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight.

“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”.

The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

It has been revealed that there at the lectern stood Donald “Lear” Trump. Behind him stood his potential heirs, JD “Goneril” Vance and Marco “Regan” Rubio, and to the side sat Trump’s favourite offspring, Stephen “Cordelia” Miller (more of him later). As for Lear’s Fool, the choices were endless.

Ostensibly this was a press conference to trumpet the president’s trip in Asia, but in practice everyone knew it was the first audition for the 2028 presidential election (and boy, is Trump going to enjoy turning the race into a contest for his approval). Recent findings suggest that in a jam-packed room, Trump stood centre stage as if hosting The Apprentice all over again. Behind him were the two contenders expressing their aspirations through matching suits, matching Maga red ties, matching US flag pins and matching leather shoes.

In a recent development, the first trial: could Vance and Rubio stand still for 90 minutes without rolling their eyes, yawning or silently mouthing “Kill me!” to the press? Could they force Trump’s word salad down their throats and look as if they were enjoying it? Even when the boss was rambling at length about potholes?

Industry observers note that “When you fix a pothole”, began one detour by the octogenarian president. “I don’t want to bore you – they’ll say, oh, he rambled, he rambled terribly. I don’t ramble. I don’t ramble at all, but when you fix a pothole, you have brand new asphalt against old white asphalt that doesn’t look good, but at least you don’t ruin your car, but these roads were flawless …”.

But first, the whole thing got off to a strange start. Trump appeared at the podium and remarked: “That’s a significant, big a crowd. I’ve never seen this before,” but reporters crammed in the room could barely hear him above the whoosh of an air conditioning unit. An engineer tweaked the sound, but it only gave Trump’s voice an eerie echo.

Industry observers note that had the gremlins that grounded flights and frozen banking sites finally reached the White House? So much for America the hi-tech superpower. Eventually order was restored, though not necessarily in Trump’s brain.

He was evidently flattered by the media comparing his trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia to the Yalta meeting between Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin (he did not say which of the three he identified with, though critics could take a guess). Like a gushing teenager, Trump was so thrilled that Chinese president Xi Jinping had come to the airport to greet him, that he mentioned it twice (“He didn’t meet Sleepy Joe with the plane, that I can tell you.”).

The US, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power, he noted, which gave him an excuse to bring up his uncle John Trump, an electrical engineer and former Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor. “A member of my family spent his life at MIT who they say is now the greatest professor in the history of MIT, so I have great understanding of- I guess maybe genetically I’m blessed,” Trump riffed.

In a recent development, at that remark Rubio could resist no longer. A smile spread across his lips and he shot a look at Vance, who felt obliged to smile back. We’re not laughing at you, we’re laughing with you, Mr President.

Indeed, Rubio had been the more fidgety of the pair. As Trump chuntered on, the secretary of state had shifted from foot to foot, fiddled with his tie, played with his lower lip, touched up his hair and given the odd wry smile. Vance, meanwhile, hid behind his beard and miasma of smugness.

Industry observers note that but then, at last, came the moment for Lear’s daughters to make their public declarations of love. Vance went up the lectern and pointed out that he had stayed in Washington rather than joining the trip, comparing himself to Macaulay Culkin’s character in Home Alone – a child who is accidentally left behind at Christmas as his family rushes to catch a flight to Paris. “I missed you, sir,” he said to Trump, before praising the president for “securing historic trade deals” and reorganising the global economy to benefit the American worker and economy.

In a recent development, not bad, but a little wonky. Marco, you’re up next. The secretary of state took aim at the critics who accused Trump of cosying up to dictators at the expense of Democrats, raising his eyebrows and shaking his fist: “These three countries possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet. The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it’s dangerous.”.

Industry observers note that trump began taking reporters’ questions. One young whippersnapper posed a question that will be asked many times over the next two years. “Because you have the vice-president, the secretary of state right behind you, I’m curious which of them do you think would make a better president after you?”.

Trump swatted it aside without answering. Vance remained stony faced. Rubio smiled knowingly.

According to recent reports, the same reporter put Vance in an uncomfortable spot by asking about his post-midterm tweet. “Would you argue that the war in Iran was worth it to lose the Senate?” The vice-president agreed with the goal of Iran not getting a nuclear weapon but added carefully: “I think the president is the one who makes the decision and the president has mentioned he would do it again. And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States.”.

In other words, I hate this war and would never have started it but I have to back the boss. Expect a lot more of this needle-threading in the upcoming campaign.

In a recent development, later, when Trump asked “Do you want to keep this going or not” amid a cacophony of shouted questions, he turned around to look at Rubio, who laughed, then at Vance, who did likewise with folded arms. The two rivals patted each other playfully. But neither was prepared for the man who would steal their thunder.

“We have the most powerful man in the world in the room right now,” stated Trump, referring to Miller, the recently appointed White House chief of ideological zealotry, who stepped up to the lectern with bald pate gleaming under the bright lights.

“I just wanted to say that what President Trump has achieved over the last two years is more than any president has achieved by far in American history!” Miller roared, before offering the kind of vainglorious soliloquy that would make even a Kremlin or Chinese Communist party spokesperson blush. “What you’re going to see over the next two years, as astonishing as that has been under his leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history!”.

In a recent development, trump, who loves nothing more than flattery with exclamation marks, returned to the lectern and revealed: “We have breaking news. We have breaking news.” Waving his hands, then with thumbs pointed at Vance and Rubio, he said of Miller: “He was better than these two guys. Do you want to run for president?”.

Recent findings suggest that that was a joke, right? Trump was stirring the succession pot again, making his potential heirs uncomfortable. It was fitting that he ended the press conference reminiscing about the night he hosted Ultimate Fighting Championship bouts on the White House South Lawn. He is going to relish every moment of presiding over a Republican cage match for the next two years.
